What is your operating system?

What version of Thunderbird?

Who is your email provider?

Is this an IMAP account or POP3?

How long has this been going on?

What is your anti-virus, if any?

Error messages like this can have a few potential causes. The most common one is the anti-virus, which can take hold of your folder file and not let go. This can be tested by temporarily disabling the AV, by creating an exception for your Thunderbird Profile, or (assuming Windows) restarting the computer in Safe Mode with Networking, which temporarily disables the AV.

It could also be caused by a server problem, which could also account for you being repeatedly asked for your password. This is usually temporary and will go away when the server admins fix it.

There are also reports of similar errors caused by a corrupt message on the server. If you can narrow down the time frame when this started, you might use the provider's web mail interface to identify the bad message and delete it from there, which could allow downloads to happen again.

content:
First, if you click your name on the line, "Question Owner', it opens to a page showing all prior threads, so that post that solved the issue a couple of years ago would be there.

Second, if thunderbird does start, try this to retrieve password:

  1. click settings>privacy&security
  2. click to savedpasswords and then show passwords. That will let you retrieve what thunderbird stored. I suggest trying his email id and that password on web account to see if it works. That would also let you possibly see his mail. If successful in this, many email providers allow an account to forward copies to another account. If true for that provider, you could set to send all future mail to your account.

If thunderbird starts somewhat, but messages for account can't be viewed, you could try this:

  1. start thunderbird on his computer
  2. click help>troubleshootinginformation
  3. scroll to 'profile folder' and click 'open folder'
  4. click the Mail account and then the POP account folder
  5. now, search everywhere in that folder for twin file sets, such as inbox, inbox.msf, sent, sent..msf, etc. the msf files are of no use, but the others have the email content.
  6. repeat the search process at Mail\Local Folders for any messages he may have saved away from the account
  7. now, COPY (not move) all such files to external media
  8. now, on YOUR computer, install the addon, importexporttools NG
  9. click to Local Folders
  10. rightclick and select the importexport option to import mbox file
  11. when file manager opens, locate one of the files exported to external media an click OK.
  12. repeat the process for all remaining files and you should see all of his message folders' contents.

If the above info about passwords worked, you could now create his account on your computer.

Let me know how it goes.

I have to wonder if you have message filtering via the quick filter toolbar enabled. First make sure the bar is enabled (ctrl+shift+K) check that none of the filtering buttons are enabled, like "unread" or "starred" that would make the message appear in the MSF but not in the UI.

Just a thought on filters, please check out the following.

Enable 'Menu Bar' toolbar if not enabled :

  • Menu App icon (3 lines) > View > Toolbars > select 'Menu Bar

Using the 'Menu Bar' toolbar Please check:

  • 'View' > 'Threads' > select 'All' - that is the default setting you ideally need to use.

If anything else is selected eg: 'Unread' then uncheck it.

However, just as a test - it's worth selecting: 'Ignored threads' (you can uncheck later) Then not only should all emails be displayed but it may also reveal if any had been set as 'ignored' and hidden from view. It's easy to press the K key and not realise you have set a thread to be ignored. Info on ignored threads:

  • https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/ignore-threads
